newsitem.title: INDIA: No decision yet on Indian oil prices - UNI.
newsitem.headline: No decision yet on Indian oil prices - UNI.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister I.K. Gujral, met the finance and petroleum ministers on Thursday on measures to plug a mounting oil subsidy bill but no decision was made to raise domestic oil prices, United News of India (UNI) said.

UNI reported earlier that the Petroleum Ministry has recommended that the cabinet approve a 15-20 percent hike in state-controlled prices of diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), and to leave prices of gasoline and kerosene unchanged.
The newsagency in its later despatch said the petroleum ministry had been pressing the finance ministry for cut in import duties on crude and petroleum products.
Junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu attended Thursday's talks with Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P.Chidambaram.

Both Gujral and Chidmabaram have said the government must decide soon how to pay off money owed to oil companies, which totalled 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March, for selling subsidised petroleum products below market prices.
UNI said Thursday's meeting was inconclusive and further discussions would be held before a final decision was taken.
